extends.rule: Protocol v2 copies the frozen v1 contract and changes only the explicitly encoded RLE extension points; v1 sources, generated outputs, and fixtures remain authoritative and immutable.

compatibility.unknown_version: reject the candidate before interpreting its payload and make no state change
compatibility.unknown_frame_kind: reject the candidate before waiting for its declared payload and make no state change
compatibility.unknown_command_kind: command kinds are request frame kinds; reject an unknown request frame kind
compatibility.unknown_checksum: reject the candidate before waiting for its declared payload
compatibility.reserved_fields: all fields still reserved by protocol v2 and all reserved request-mask bits are zero on send and rejected when nonzero
compatibility.unknown_capability_bits: bits outside the generated protocol-v2 capability mask are rejected in an INFO response
compatibility.default_client: Existing clients and default RAW configurations continue to speak protocol v1 and never infer or request compression.
compatibility.version_selection: Only an explicit RLE_AUTO request enters protocol-v2 negotiation; the host obtains a protocol-v2 INFO response and requires RLE_STREAMING before sending CONFIGURE.
compatibility.v1_isolation: A protocol-v1 INFO response never advertises RLE_STREAMING, and no protocol-v1 header, payload, constant, manifest, or fixture is reinterpreted as protocol v2.

header.encoding: fixed-width unsigned integers in little-endian byte order

trailer.coverage: all 44 header bytes followed by every payload byte, starting at magic offset 0 and excluding all 4 trailer bytes

limits.data_frame_bytes_semantics: the configured wire maximum and the exact full RAW data-frame length

counter_semantics.stats_generation: nonzero u32 incremented modulo 2^32 with zero skipped whenever counters reset
counter_semantics.overflow: cumulative u64 and u32 counters saturate at the maximum value of their wire type; current u16 depths are gauges and u16 high-water fields remain monotonic until reset
counter_semantics.wrapping_identities: data-frame sequences wrap modulo 2^32; run_id and stats_generation advance modulo 2^32 while skipping zero
counter_semantics.reset_constraint: RESET_STATS is accepted only in IDLE or CONFIGURED after raw, packer, packet, and data-transport ownership is quiescent and the older control-response queue is empty; BUSY and INVALID_STATE responses preserve every counter and the generation
counter_semantics.adc_frames_emitted: complete ADC_DATA frames admitted to the USB transmit path
counter_semantics.gpio_frames_emitted: complete GPIO_DATA frames admitted to the USB transmit path
counter_semantics.adc_items_dropped: ADC sample pairs not emitted because of acquisition, queue, or transport loss
counter_semantics.adc_pairs_captured: complete and stopped-partial ADC pair instants accepted by at least one converter DMA path
counter_semantics.adc_pairs_delivered: complete dual-converter pairs leased to the cooperative ADC packetizer
counter_semantics.adc_pairs_framed: complete dual-converter pairs admitted to ADC_DATA frames
counter_semantics.adc_pairs_transmitted: complete dual-converter pairs completely written through the CDC transport
counter_semantics.adc_raw_pairs_lost: ADC pair instants discarded before framing because of conversion/DMA evidence, ring pressure, or STOP partial progress
counter_semantics.adc_raw_ring_overruns: complete paired ADC DMA major loops redirected to the fixed overflow sink
counter_semantics.adc_etc_error_events: ADC_ETC overwrite/error interrupt events attributed to the active acquisition epoch
counter_semantics.adc_dma_error_events: eDMA channel error events attributed to the active acquisition epoch
counter_semantics.gpio_items_dropped: packed eight-pin GPIO sample instants not emitted because of acquisition, queue, or transport loss
counter_semantics.gpio_samples_captured: complete and stopped-partial GPIO2_PSR sample instants accepted by the raw acquisition owner
counter_semantics.gpio_samples_packed: raw GPIO2_PSR sample instants converted to the one-byte D6-through-D13 wire layout
counter_semantics.gpio_samples_framed: packed GPIO sample instants admitted to complete GPIO_DATA frames
counter_semantics.gpio_samples_transmitted: packed GPIO sample instants completely written through the CDC transport
counter_semantics.gpio_raw_samples_lost: GPIO sample instants discarded before packing because the raw DMA ring overflowed or STOP ended a partial major loop
counter_semantics.gpio_packer_samples_dropped: GPIO sample instants discarded inside the pre-packet packed-buffer owner
counter_semantics.gpio_raw_ring_overruns: complete raw DMA major loops redirected to the fixed overflow sink
counter_semantics.gpio_resource_conflicts: physical START attempts rejected before register mutation because a reserved PIT/XBAR/DMAMUX/eDMA resource was already active
counter_semantics.adc_cache_dma_discards: cooperative ADC cache-discard calls completed before a buffer or sink became DMA-writeable
counter_semantics.adc_cache_cpu_invalidations: cooperative ADC cache-invalidate calls completed before a paired buffer became CPU-readable
counter_semantics.gpio_cache_dma_discards: cooperative GPIO cache-discard calls completed before a buffer or sink became DMA-writeable
counter_semantics.gpio_cache_cpu_invalidations: cooperative GPIO cache-invalidate calls completed before a raw buffer became CPU-readable
counter_semantics.packet_pressure_evictions: complete unsent data frames evicted under packet-pool pressure
counter_semantics.packet_capacity_drops_without_evictable_: new complete source frames dropped because every packet buffer was pinned or producer-owned
counter_semantics.adc_packet_filling_depth: producer-owned incomplete ADC packet buffers at the STATUS snapshot
counter_semantics.gpio_packet_filling_depth: producer-owned incomplete GPIO packet buffers at the STATUS snapshot
counter_semantics.adc_frames_dropped_after_framing: ADC frames dropped after becoming a complete READY frame, including the post-promotion subset
counter_semantics.adc_frames_dropped_after_promotion: ADC frames dropped after entering the USB-facing transmit queue but before byte zero was accepted
counter_semantics.gpio_frames_dropped_after_framing: GPIO frames dropped after becoming a complete READY frame, including the post-promotion subset
counter_semantics.gpio_frames_dropped_after_promotion: GPIO frames dropped after entering the USB-facing transmit queue but before byte zero was accepted
counter_semantics.gpio_buffers_completed: complete GPIO raw DMA buffers made CPU-readable
counter_semantics.gpio_buffers_acquired: complete GPIO raw DMA buffers leased once to the cooperative packer
counter_semantics.gpio_buffers_released: GPIO raw DMA buffer leases returned to DMA ownership
counter_semantics.gpio_samples_delivered: GPIO sample instants leased from complete raw buffers to the cooperative packer
counter_semantics.gpio_stop_samples_discarded: GPIO sample instants captured in a stopped partial DMA major loop and deliberately discarded
counter_semantics.gpio_frames_produced: complete logical GPIO frame intervals consumed or classified as pre-packet loss by the packer
counter_semantics.gpio_samples_produced: unique GPIO sample instants consumed or classified as source gaps by the packer
counter_semantics.gpio_frames_packed: complete retained GPIO frame intervals converted into packed-buffer ownership
counter_semantics.gpio_duplicate_samples_ignored: stale or overlapping GPIO sample instants rejected by packer chronology checks
counter_semantics.adc_frames_consumed: complete paired ADC DMA buffers consumed by the cooperative packetizer
counter_semantics.adc_pairs_consumed: paired ADC sample instants consumed by the cooperative packetizer
counter_semantics.adc_raw_gap_pairs: missing ADC pair instants inferred before packet ownership
counter_semantics.adc_raw_drop_pairs_projected: raw ADC gap pairs already represented by packet sequence/drop counters
counter_semantics.gpio_raw_drop_samples_projected: raw GPIO loss already represented by packet sequence/drop counters
counter_semantics.gpio_packer_drop_samples_projected: pre-packet GPIO packer loss already represented by packet sequence/drop counters

configuration_semantics.bootstrap_checksum: Every request and response frame uses ADLER32, including INFO and CONFIGURE; only data frames use the configured data checksum algorithm.
configuration_semantics.checksum_transition: A device returns BUSY instead of applying CONFIGURE while complete data frames from the prior configuration remain queued.
configuration_semantics.stream_mask: a subset of ADC/GPIO; zero is reserved for the control-only profile and otherwise at least one advertised stream is required
configuration_semantics.profile_matrix: INFO publishes supported_configuration_mask so a host validates an exact source/stream pair instead of assuming every advertised stream and source can be combined. Protocol v2 retains the v1 rule that one source is selected for every enabled stream, so per-stream physical/synthetic mixing is not representable and is rejected atomically.
configuration_semantics.encoding_negotiation: RAW preserves protocol-v1 behavior. RLE_AUTO is explicit, valid only in protocol v2, and accepted only after INFO advertises RLE_STREAMING; CONFIGURE and START echo the exact applied encoding.

control_only_profile.availability: only on milestone firmware whose INFO supported_stream_mask is zero
control_only_profile.purpose: exercise CONFIGURE, START, GET_STATUS, RESET_STATS, PING, and STOP before acquisition is implemented

checksum.coverage: all transmitted header bytes followed by the encoded payload, excluding the trailer
validation_order: validate bounded header and transmitted lengths
validate checksum over transmitted header and encoded payload

firmware_diagnostic_semantics.commands_rejected: parser candidate rejections plus typed command errors
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.bad_checksums: parser candidates rejected because the trailer disagrees with the checksum algorithm selected by the header
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.bad_lengths: parser candidates rejected for magic, size, or length invariants
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.bad_types: parser candidates rejected for an unknown or non-request frame kind
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.bad_versions: parser candidates rejected for an unsupported protocol version
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.bad_flags: parser candidates rejected for reserved or illegal frame flags
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.bad_payloads: parser candidates rejected for reserved fields or command-specific payload invariants
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.bad_request_ids: parser or semantic command rejections for zero or duplicate request identifiers
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.timeouts: bounded firmware transport operations that reached their deadline
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.partial_usb_writes: USB writes that accepted fewer bytes than requested without implying a framing error
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.responses_queued: complete checksummed control responses admitted to the bounded response queue
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.responses_completed: complete control responses fully written through CDC
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.response_queue_rejections: response enqueue attempts rejected for invalid framing, kind, or unavailable capacity
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.response_reservations_abandoned: dequeued commands whose reserved response slot could not be fulfilled
firmware_diagnostic_semantics.overflow: all firmware diagnostic counters saturate at their native unsigned maximum

checksum_benchmark.semantics: The optional command is valid only in IDLE. Each timed checksum interval excludes interrupt service, subtracts calibrated counter/read overhead, and is shorter than one 32-bit DWT wrap. Cold OCRAM cache maintenance is timed separately. The command never resets or mutates acquisition counters.

gpio_clock_diagnostic.semantics: The optional command is valid only in IDLE and runs one bounded PIT/XBARA/eDMA measurement without remapping GPIO pads or producing data frames. Requested rates must divide the fixed 24 MHz PIT clock exactly and may not exceed the immutable 4 MHz production rate. scheduled_event_count is derived from measured DWT elapsed cycles; dma_sample_count comes independently from the eDMA major-loop counter.

gpio_capture.semantics: Physical protocol-v2 GPIO mode accepts GPIO alone or alongside the ADC stream under the one shared hardware schedule. One decoded packed byte represents D6 through D13 as bits 0 through 7. Raw DMA and packed CPU rings are fixed-capacity and every frame timestamp is derived from its decoded source sample index relative to one START epoch.

combined_acquisition.semantics: All six nonempty protocol-v2 source/stream profiles are supported. Physical ADC and GPIO share one PIT-derived epoch and three fixed eDMA channels; synthetic profiles retain the independent full-rate USB/host baseline.

gpio_capture_diagnostic.semantics: The optional empty-request command is valid only in fully quiescent IDLE. Fixture policy is compiled into the artifact and cannot be changed by the request. The response identifies whether non-driving capture, an explicitly safe self-driven sweep, or declared fixture stimulus was selected and reports exact register/count/electrical-claim evidence.

adc_initialization.semantics: Both ADC modules are configured independently for synchronous 37.5 MHz high-speed conversion, no hardware averaging, and the shortest three-ADCK sample setting. Calibration starts only after route/configuration validation and is bounded independently per converter by both the 600 MHz DWT deadline and a finite poll limit. VREFH/VREFL range values are nominal board metadata, not calibrated voltage claims. Twelve bits remains primary; ten bits may be selected only by the explicit completed timing/error fallback gate.

adc_trigger.semantics: PIT0 divides the verified 24 MHz PERCLK root by six for the exact 4 MHz GPIO master. Chained PIT1 divides those expirations by four for one exact 1 MHz event fanned out through distinct XBAR outputs to asynchronous ADC_ETC queues 0 and 4. With PRE_DIVIDER=0, raw initial delays 0 and 75 have effective delays of 1 and 76 IPG cycles, an exact 75-cycle or 500 ns difference. The bounded DWT diagnostic measures relative conversion-completion interrupt timing only; it is not analog aperture evidence.

flags.name: SYNTHETIC
flags.description: Data payload was produced by the deterministic test source.

flags.name: GAP_BEFORE
flags.description: At least one item or frame was dropped before this data frame.

flags.name: EPOCH_START
flags.description: This is the first frame for this stream in a new run.

flags.name: OVERRUN_BEFORE
flags.description: Firmware lost one or more logical items before this frame; GAP_BEFORE is also required.

flags.name: RESPONSE_ERROR
flags.description: The response prefix reports a nonzero error code.

checksum_algorithms.name: NONE_RESERVED
checksum_algorithms.description: Reserved invalid value; every v2 frame has a checksum.

checksum_algorithms.name: ADLER32
checksum_algorithms.description: RFC 1950 Adler-32 with initial value 1 and modulus 65521; fixed control bootstrap and the Phase 05 selected production data default.

checksum_algorithms.name: CRC32C
checksum_algorithms.description: CRC-32C (Castagnoli), reflected input/output, initial value 0xffffffff, and final XOR 0xffffffff; retained for negotiated data and captured benchmark evidence.

checksum_algorithms.name: CRC32_ISO_HDLC
checksum_algorithms.description: CRC-32/ISO-HDLC, reflected input/output, initial value 0xffffffff, and final XOR 0xffffffff; retained for negotiated data and captured benchmark evidence.

configuration_encoding.name: RAW
configuration_encoding.description: Transmit every data frame as the unchanged raw logical-item payload.

configuration_encoding.name: RLE_AUTO
configuration_encoding.description: Evaluate canonical RLE independently for every frame and select it only when the complete RLE wire frame is strictly smaller than RAW.

frame_encoding.name: RAW
frame_encoding.description: The transmitted payload is the unchanged raw logical-item sequence.

frame_encoding.name: RLE
frame_encoding.description: The transmitted payload is a canonical sequence of frame-local RLE records.
